chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim, from his father, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is there an Eid for the Muslims other than the day of Friday, and Al-Adha, and Al-Fitr?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, the greatest of them in sanctity.' I said, 'And which Eid is it? May I be your sacrifice.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The day in which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) appointed the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said:
Whoever I am his Mawla, Ali is his Mawla.

I said, 'And which day is it?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'What do you do with the day? Indeed, the year circulates. But it is the eighteenth of Dhi al-Hijjah.' So I said, 'And what is befitting for us to do on that day?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You remember Allah, Exalted is His Remembrance, therein with fasting, and worship, and remembrance of Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad. For indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) bequeathed to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) that he should take that day as an Eid. And thus the Prophets (peace be upon them) used to do; they would bequeath to their successors with that, so they would take it as an Eid.'

key_terms.مَنْ كُنْتُ مَوْلَاهُ فَعَلِيٌّ مَوْلَاه: Whoever I am his Mawla, Ali is his Mawla

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 18th of Dhi al-Hijjah in Shia Islam and how should it be observed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the 18th of Dhi al-Hijjah as the 'Greater Eid' (Eid al-Akbar), commemorating the Ghadir Khumm event where the Prophet Muhammad appointed Imam Ali as his successor. It highlights the Shia practice of combining fasting with worship and remembrance, linking this tradition to the precedent set by previous Prophets who designated days for their successors, thereby affirming the continuity of divine leadership (Imamate).

en.hubeali: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Abdul Rahman Bin Salim, from his father who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is there an Eid for the Muslims apart from the day of Friday, and Al-Azha, and Al-Fitr?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, one greater than that in sanctity’. I said, ‘And which Eid is it, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The day during which Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> nominated Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> and said: ‘The one whose Master I<sup>saww</sup> was, so Ali<sup>asws</sup> is his Master’.

I said, ‘And which day was it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What would you do with the (particular) day as the year circulates. But, it was the 18<sup>th</sup> of Zilhajj’. So I said, ‘And is befitting for us that we should be doing during that day?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Mentioning Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Mighty is His<sup>azwj</sup> Mention, during it with the Fasting, and the worship, and the mention of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> and the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> bequeathed Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> should be taking it as an Eid, and similar to that is what the Prophets<sup>as</sup> used to bequeath their<sup>as</sup> successors<sup>as</sup> with that, therefore take it as an Eid’.
en.sarwar: 3. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim from his father who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Are there for Muslims other ‘Id besides, Friday, the tenth of the month of Dhul Hajjah and the first day of the month of Shawwal?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘Yes, there is such a day, in fact, it is of greater importance.’ I then asked, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, which days are they?’ He replied, ‘One is the day during which the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, announced the appointment of ’Amir al-Mu’minin (as the executor of his will), saying, “Whoever’ s guardian I am, Ali also is his guardian.’”
I then asked, ‘Which day is this day?’

He replied, ‘What do you have to do with the day; the year goes around, however, it is the eighteenth of the month of Dhul Hajjah.’ I then asked, ‘What should we do during this day?’ He replied, ‘You should pay attention to Allah, majestic is whose mention, by fasting, worshipping and speaking of Muhammad and his family, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause. The Messenger of Allah advised ’Amir al-Mu’minin to celebrate this day as ‘Id. This is what the prophets would do. They would advise the executors (of their wills) to celebrate this day as a day of ’Id.’”
